subject: Post-call: subprocessor & data handling follow-up (PII / retention / residency)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: subprocessor & data handling follow-up (PII / retention / residency)

Thanks again for the call earlier, Ida — great to meet you. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the key items and next steps so your security/procurement teams have something concrete to review. TL;DR: Redwood can support EU data residency for inference logs/contexts via our Private deployment or by region-restricting hosted endpoints; we also offer configurable retention and subprocessor transparency.

Notes from the call:
- Data types: you confirmed that ACME will send customer PII (names, emails, support transcripts) to Redwood for model-driven features.
- Retention: you asked about default retention for request/response logs (KV/cache, telemetry, and full transcripts). Our hosted defaults are 90 days for request/response logs and 365 days for aggregated telemetry; we can shorten retention or disable persistent storage for sensitive routes.
- Logging/telemetry: runtime telemetry (metrics, error traces) is collected for service health. We do not surface raw customer prompt/response text to telemetry providers by default.
- Subprocessors: core infra is on AWS (us-east-1 / eu-west-1), optional GCP for some customers. Observability vendors we use: Datadog (metrics/alerts), Sentry (errors), Segment (opt-in analytics pipeline for product usage). Marketplace flows (cloud marketplace metering) can create billing metadata flows — we can redact payloads as required.
- Residency options: Hosted (region pinning) vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) — Private gives strongest guarantee for residency and network isolation.

Attachments included for your review: Redwood_DPA_draft.pdf (our standard DPA), subprocessors_20260302.csv (current list + controls), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 scope summary).

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll send the DPA + subprocessor list for your legal/security review (attached).
2) Alex will follow up with a short note on telemetry flows and exactly which elements are sent to each vendor.
3) If you want stricter retention/residency, we can put together a Private deployment quote — I can loop in Solutions if helpful.
4) Schedule a 30-min follow-up (security + procurement).

Let me know if I missed anything.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our side before we loop Legal/Security: 

1) For the telemetry vendors (Datadog/Sentry/Segment) — can you confirm whether any raw prompt or response text is ever forwarded to them? If so, is that by default or opt-in?
2) For marketplace billing flows, you mentioned we can redact payloads — is that a real-time redaction or post-hoc? Who has access to the full payloads (Redwood ops, third-party?).
3) If we choose an EU-only residency (eu-west-1), will any of the service logs or backups be replicated outside the EU?
4) We'll want to see the DPA redlines and a current subprocessor list. Please include any vendor contact or SOC2 evidence you have.

Also: our procurement team prefers vendor answers in writing (short Q/A or yes/no table) to speed review. Would you be able to provide a short subprocessor Q&A?

Can we schedule a follow-up next week (security + procurement) — include security@acme-corp.com on the invite.

Best,

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T19:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: subprocessor & data handling follow-up (PII / retention / residency)

Hi Ida — Alex here (infra product). Quick answers to your bullets below, wanted to be explicit so procurement/security has actionable answers: 

1) Raw prompt/response forwarding to telemetry vendors: DEFAULT = no. We never send full prompt/response text to Datadog/Sentry for customers on standard hosted plans. Error traces include anonymized request IDs and stack traces; if a customer opts into deep debugging/trace capture, there is an opt-in pipeline (explicit flag) that can forward redacted excerpts for Sentry. Segment is opt-in for usage analytics and is never used to store customer content; only metadata/events are sent (no PII text). We can provide configuration flags to turn off any of these integrations entirely.

2) Marketplace billing flows: metering records contain usage metadata (tokens, durations) but do not include prompt contents. Redaction is applied at the service edge before payloads are forwarded for metering. Access to raw payloads is restricted to the customer's Private deployment or dedicated instances; hosted logs are accessible to a minimal ops group for incident response under strict controls and audit logging.

3) EU-only residency: For hosted region pinning to eu-west-1 we ensure compute and persistent storage for that tenant remain in eu-west-1. Backups and cold archives are retained in-region; we do not replicate backups outside the EU unless contractually required (and we will not for EU-data residency customers). We can provide an addendum guaranteeing no cross-border replication.

4) DPA & SOC2: Marissa attached the DPA draft and SOC2 summary. For SOC2 full reports we can provide the cert or a SOC2 Type II report under NDA — typically 3 business days to share after NDA.

5) Subprocessor Q/A: We can produce a short table: vendor, function, data types accessed, access controls, encryption at rest/in transit, contact/SOC2 status. I'll put together a one-page Q&A and send it by EOD tomorrow.

If you prefer a Private deployment to completely avoid hosted subprocessors, we can scope that as well — solutions team times/quote if requested.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Martinez | Product, Infra 
alex.martinez@redwood.com
